title: What a capability CONSUMES from the host's measured reading (data, never code)
description: A detector emits a fact; this is the other half -- a capability declaring that one named fact MEANS something to it, and what its absence is to be called. Both halves are data: which fact feeds what, and the words an absence is stated in, are declared here and nowhere in any interpreter. A host that emits a fact no row names is not an error -- nobody declared a use for it, which is a smaller statement than a defect. The rows carry no command, no default and no fallback: what a reading says is the host's, and the only thing this document adds to it is a meaning and the sentence to print when the host said nothing.

means.description: What this reading IS, in the words a reader of the projection meets. Never what it is used for by some other machine -- a meaning that only makes sense to the consumer is a meaning the host cannot check.

reads.description: The one fact this row consumes, spelled exactly as a detector emits it. BOUND means the recorded reading carries that key; anything else is the gap below. There is no second fact, no `equals`, and no default: a row that could fall back to a value nobody measured would print a plausible sentence about a host that never said it.

gap.description: The words the surface states when the fact is absent, written as a DECLARED GAP and never as an empty value, a zero or a silence. It is authored here rather than composed by an interpreter because an absence is a statement about this host, and the sentence that states it is the declaration's to make.

proves_a_change.description: This reading is the command the host declares for proving a change: what `prove` runs when no area declares a proof and no MUST names a command. At most one reading says so.
